content.text:
Confirmed — that's purely an import path change from the package reorganization. The logic bug is isolated to the `DownloadManagerInterface.java` edit within the same commit.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 991e500e28c9e21d28512418a0e0f4fae62560b9

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit adds `MainActivity.onDestroy()` calling a new `DownloadManagerInterface.destroy(Context)` method that unregisters `downloadCompletionReceiver` and nulls the singleton `instance`. This is the signature of a fix for "a `BroadcastReceiver`/singleton was registered but never unregistered, leaking a `Context`." I traced the full history of `DownloadManagerInterface.java` (via its two file paths, before and after a package rename) looking specifically at `registerReceiver`/`registerReceiver(context)`/`unregisterReceiver`/`instance =` occurrences across every revision.

**(2) The introducing change:** Commit `991e500` (2016-10-17, part of a package-reorganization commit renaming `data/DownloadManagerInterface.java` → `data/downloadmanager/DownloadManagerInterface.java`) changed:
```java
private final Context context;      // removed field, previously set to context.getApplicationContext()
...
instance.registerReceiver();         // old: no-arg, used this.context (app context)
...
private void registerReceiver() {
    context.registerReceiver(...);   // old: registered with application context
}
```
into:
```java
instance.registerReceiver(context); // new: passes the raw context argument from init(context)
...
private void registerReceiver(Context context) {
    context.registerReceiver(...);   // new: registers with whatever context init() was called with
}
```
`init(Context context)` is called from `MainActivity.onCreate(this)`, i.e. with the **Activity** instance, not the application context (only the constructor's `new DownloadManagerInterface(context.getApplicationContext())` used the app context — for the *other* fields — but the receiver registration itself now uses the raw Activity context). Because `init()` only creates the singleton once (`if (instance == null)`), the `BroadcastReceiver` ends up permanently registered against the very first `MainActivity` instance ever created, and it is never unregistered anywhere. That keeps that first `Activity` instance alive for the lifetime of the process — a classic context leak — which is exactly what the fix commit's `destroy()`/`onDestroy()` addition resolves (unregister the receiver and clear the singleton so a fresh instance/registration can occur).

**(3) Supporting evidence:** Prior to `991e500`, `registerReceiver()` took no parameter and used the internally stored application context, so no leak existed. `991e500` is the sole commit in the file's history that switched the receiver-registration call site to use the raw `Context` argument instead of the application context, and no subsequent commit before the bug-fix added any corresponding unregister/cleanup logic — that gap is precisely what `8eeef35` fixes. The only other file touched by `991e500`, `MainActivity.java`, changed nothing but an import path (due to the package rename), confirming the behavioral change is fully contained in the `DownloadManagerInterface.java` edit of this commit.

I'm fairly confident in this identification since the mechanism lines up exactly with the fix, though I can't fully rule out that an even earlier commit set up preconditions (e.g., moving `init()` calls from `SebApp` to `MainActivity` in `1eb67a2`) as a contributing factor — but that earlier move alone did not leak, since the context passed to the receiver registration was still the application context at that time.
